title: Process definition (process.yaml) v0.2.0
description: A process is a directory of configuration; process.yaml says who acts (actor) and how: on behalf of which authority (on_behalf_of, mandates), through which channels and in which roles people log in (channels, roles), whether there is a portal that has a submission recorded in a cell, which cells it merges lexostatuses from (synthesis), and which actions a handler performs in a case (handling). A process records nothing and reduces nothing itself: a cell does that, at the process's request. Paths are relative to the directory of process.yaml.

id.description: The name of the process. The runtime serves it under /processes/<id>/api/.

actor.description: The recording actor (recording_actor): a cell records for the process only in a stream with this recording_actor. On behalf of which competent authority the process acts is given by on_behalf_of, not by the actor.

origin_check.description: How strict the origin check (RFC-048) is on startup. lenient: a parameter without origin is a warning. strict: a parameter without origin is an error, because then it cannot be traced who supplies it. With strict, every synthesis source that translates also carries a legal_basis (see source.legal_basis).

mandates.description: Authorities for which the process acts under mandate (Awb 10:1 ff.). If, for a decision, the law designates an authority other than on_behalf_of, the cell records the decision only if a mandate from that authority is listed here; the gram then names the legal basis with the acting actor.

authority.description: The mandating authority, as a loaded regulation names it in competent_authority.

legal_basis.description: What the mandate rests on: <regulation>#<article>, optionally with ' lid <n>'. The article must be loaded.

channels.description: The channels through which someone logs in to the process, per id. Each channel is simulated: identification fields with a format check, no certified login and no register. The routes are /api/channels/<id>/login, /session and /logout.

synthesis.description: Lexostatuses from cells that the process merges: the portal's assessment, the offer and the trial decision. A source with case: true is a lexostatus of the case itself; the other sources name their input and parameters. None of this is recorded.

examples.description: Default data per action, for a trial setup: the frontend offers them to prefill a form or to perform the action with them directly. Each file is JSON; the runtime checks the shape on startup. None of this is recorded.

logins.description: Logins, each an object with the fields of a channel, and optionally channel (without it: the portal's only channel) and role. The label is the file name without extension.

application.description: An application: an object with external, as the portal receives it.

actions.description: Per action (the name in handling.actions) a form: an object with form, as the action receives it. A value "$today" becomes today's date when requested, so an example does not go stale (a decision or payment in the future is not a fact).

portal.description: A process with a portal allows logging in (fake eHerkenning), assessing a draft and recording a submission in a cell. Without a portal, the process does not have those routes.

cell.description: The cell in which the submission is recorded. It runs in the same runtime.

stream.description: The $id of the stream of that cell in which the portal records.

event.description: The event from that stream that becomes a submission.

rows.description: Per-row synthesis, as for the decision: table fields of the assessment lexostatus that become an array parameter, before the engine.

assessment.description: The assessment before submitting: the cell reduces the draft on trial to this lexostatus, the process merges, builds the rows, and the engine evaluates the output.

offer.description: What the portal offers: an output of the policy (for example 'aanvraag aangeboden'), executed in a run, and optionally the output of the same regulation that gives the deadline. The portal shows the offer; it rejects nothing.

windows.description: An output of the same regulation: the list of windows the policy offers, if the offer article asks for a window (the parameter with origin BELANGHEBBENDE and legal basis Awb 4:2 lid 1, RFC-048). The runtime computes it in a separate run on today's date, without parameters, and runs the offer once per window. Which windows exist is policy, not configuration.

start.description: An output of the same regulation: the first day of a window, computed with only the chosen window as parameter. The offer for a window that has yet to start has the sources evaluated as of that day (as_of); without start, they are evaluated as of today. Requires windows.

opening.description: An output of the same regulation: the first day on which an application for a window can come in, computed with only the window as parameter. The counter does not accept a receipt date before that day. Requires windows.

form.description: Optional form file for labels and order. It never determines behavior.

source.description: A lexostatus of a cell. Without url, the transport is internal: the cell runs in the same runtime. With url, the query goes over HTTP to <url>/cells/<cell>/api/lexostatus/<lexostatus>. With case: true, it is a lexostatus of the case itself, in the cell in which the process records, with root as its only input: the decision queries it with the root and takes over all its parameters and extra fields. Such a source names no input, parameters or extra fields.

regulation.description: Instead of cell: the consumer's own policy, computed by the engine (note on source and gram id). lexostatus is then the article (<regulation>#<article>), input are the parameters and extra_fields the outputs; a register that queries that policy is provided by the deployment (CELL_REGISTERS).

case.description: A lexostatus of the case itself (see above).

input.description: Per input of the source lexostatus: which field the value comes from (lexostatus and field), or a fixed value (value). A field comes from a lexostatus of the case (for the assessment: the assessment lexostatus; a parameter or an extra field), or from the response of an earlier source in the list that passes that field on under extra_fields; that source may itself wait for an earlier source.

value.description: A fixed value, such as the body whose register is queried.

extra_fields.description: Extra fields from this source's response that are not parameters but input for a later source in the list (for example a name for a registration number). They do not go to the engine.

parameters.description: The parameters this source supplies, explicitly and without wildcards: a list if the source supplies them under the same name, or, per name at the source, the name at the consumer. Each name at the consumer is a parameter of an article under the assessment, the decision or the offer, and comes from only one source. May be empty only if the source passes on extra_fields.

oneOf.description: Per name the source supplies: the parameter name under which the consumer asks for the fact. The source speaks the language of its own law and supplies the name as a parameter or as an extra field; the translation to the consumer's parameters belongs with the consumer (synthesis at the consumer).

legal_basis.description: What the translation of this source rests on: the articles that ask for the fact at the consumer under its name and have the source supply it, and that carry a fixed value in the input (such as which body's register). On startup: every article is loaded and the paragraph (lid) exists. With origin_check: strict, every source that translates (a name at the consumer that differs from the name at the source, or a fixed value) has a legal_basis.

roles.description: Who logs in to the process, per role: through which channel, and which route groups the role may use (portal: form, assessment, offer and submit; handling: worklist, case, trial decision and decision; counter: enter an application that came in by another route). Without roles there is no login.

label.description: How the frontend names the role; without it: the id.

legal_basis.description: Why this role is allowed to do this, such as a mandate or service regulation. A decision carries it with the acting actor.

handling.description: What the handler does in the process: view the worklist, open a case and perform actions in it: on trial, and then record. What an action needs, and from whom, follows from the stage of its record event (RFC-008) and from the origin of the parameters of its article (RFC-048), not from this configuration. Requires a role with the handling route.

worklist.description: A list lexostatus (group_by: root) of the cell in which the process records.

actions.description: The actions possible in a case: the decision, the stages after it (such as the notification) and the facts of the course of the case (a request, a receipt, a payment).

rows.description: Per-row synthesis: for each row of a table field, the process queries sources with values from that row, and the columns together form an array parameter. This way the actor fills the columns it determines itself, without putting them in code.

parameter.description: The array parameter that the rows together form.

table.description: The table field that supplies the rows: a lexostatus of the case, or a source that passes the field on, and the name under which it supplies the table (a parameter or an extra field).

columns.description: Per column of the table: the name under which it goes into the parameter. A column not listed here is left out.

sources.description: Sources queried per row, in order: a source can use a column that an earlier source supplied.

input.description: Per input of the source: the value from the row (column), from a lexostatus of the case or a source that passes the field on (lexostatus and field), from the merged parameters (parameter), an output of a regulation computed with the merged parameters (regulation and output; this is how the law derives an input, such as a reference date), or a fixed value (value).

columns.description: Per name the source supplies (a parameter or an extra field): the column name under which it goes into the row.

legal_basis.description: What the translation of this source rests on, as for a synthesis source: a column named differently at the consumer than at the source, or a fixed value in the input. With origin_check: strict, required as soon as the source translates.

label.description: The name of the channel on the login screen.

explanation.description: Explanation on the login screen. The frontend itself adds that the login is simulated.

fields.description: The identification fields, in the order of the login screen.

pattern.description: A regular expression the whole value must match; without it: not empty.

check.description: elfproef: nine digits, weighted 9 through 2 and -1, with the sum divisible by 11 (like a burgerservicenummer).

message.description: The message for a value that does not match.

numeric.description: The frontend shows a numeric keyboard.

legal_basis.description: What the field rests on: the rule that defines the data item and its format, such as the number a register assigns. On startup: every article is loaded and the paragraph (lid) exists.

owner.description: The field that identifies the owner of a case: whoever follows a case must have a gram in that case with their value of this field.

intake.description: The path under $intake at which the fields arrive at the cell; without it: the id of the channel.

legal_basis.description: What the channel and its owner rest on: the rule that says by which means and on whose behalf someone logs in. On startup: every article is loaded and the paragraph (lid) exists.

on_behalf_of.description: The competent authority on whose behalf the process acts: the name as a regulation gives it in competent_authority, or a regulation of which it is the competent authority. On startup, the runtime checks that the authority occurs in a loaded regulation, uses it to find the decision if handling.decision names no regulation, and checks it against the law's authority at the decision. Required with handling.

action.description: An action in a case: the outputs of an article, computed with what the case, the synthesis and the form supply, and the event in which the cell records it. The kind follows from the event: with a stage known to the article's procedure (RFC-008), the first such action is the decision and every later stage of the same article is a follow-up to that decision (the engine executes the stage on the input of the recorded decision, with that stage's hooks); without a stage, the action records a fact that the case's lexostatuses read, and the fact counts on trial. A case can have several decisions, each from its own article (an advance, a determination, a recovery); the record event says whether a gram opens, follows or amends a decision (decision in the stream). The form is not listed here: for a decision the parameters with origin OORDEEL, for a follow-up what the stage asks for (requires), for a fact the event's $external fields that are not outputs.

name.description: The name of the action, unique within the process; the route is cases/<root>/actions/<name>.

label.description: How the frontend names the action; without it, the name.

role.description: The role allowed to perform the action: a key of roles, with the handling route. Without it: every role allowed to use handling.

decision.description: The name of the decision's action that this action belongs to, if its record event follows or amends a decision. Required for a fact that follows a decision (decision: follows, such as a payment that executes a decision: RFC-022 sec. 3.3) and for a decision that amends another decision (decision: amends, such as an amendment of a determination under Awb 4:49); the process then acts on the latest decision of that action in the case, including any amendment of it. A follow-up (a later stage of the same article) finds its decision itself; if it names one anyway, it must be that one.

decision_parameter.description: The article parameter that receives the id of the decision the action acts on (note on source and gram id): this is how the process calls its own policy that reads per decision, such as the payment administration. Wiring, not law.

regulation.description: Optional. Without this key, the article is the beschikking (produces: BESCHIKKING) for which the competent authority equals the authority the process acts for (on_behalf_of).

outputs.description: Outputs of one and the same article of the regulation. For a follow-up, these are joined by the outputs of the hooks the law fires at that stage (such as the objection period, Awb 6:8); those are not listed here, and without regulation the list may then be empty. If the event records an executogram and the article is in its legal_basis as TOETS, every boolean output counts, with the norm of that provision as legal_basis: false means it cannot be taken.

rows.description: Per-row synthesis: table fields that become an array parameter.

record.description: The cell and event in which the process has the action recorded. The event follows the case; its $external keys are outputs or fields of the form.

lexostatus_name.description: The name of a lexostatus: a name from lexostatuses.yaml, or the reading article of a lexostatus from the law (<regulation>#<article>, optionally with ' lid <n>').
